# Finding the data and the metadata {#sec-finding-data}

You need two things before downloading: the **list of run accessions**,
and a **table saying what each run is** (sample, condition, replicate,
single- or paired-end). This chapter shows three ways to get both: by
clicking, from ENA, and from the command line.

## Step 0: find the accession in the paper

Look in the **Data availability** statement, the Methods, or the last
lines of the abstract. You're looking for a `GSE`, `PRJNA`/`PRJEB`, `SRP`,
or `E-MTAB` (ArrayExpress, now BioStudies) number. If only an `E-MTAB` is given,
its raw reads are in ENA, under an `ERP`/`PRJEB` linked from the BioStudies page.

## Option A: GEO + SRA Run Selector (point and click)

1. **Open the GEO series**, e.g.
   [GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778).
   Read the summary and the overall design, and scroll down to **Samples**,
   one GSM per biological sample. The supplementary files are at the very
   bottom.
2. **Open the SRA Run Selector**. At the bottom of the GSE page, in the
   *Relations* box, follow **SRA**, then *Send to → Run Selector*. Or go
   straight to `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Traces/study/?acc=GSE52778`.
3. In Run Selector, the table has **one row per run** with the metadata as
   columns. Tick rows to select a subset (e.g. only untreated and Dex), or
   use all.
4. Download two files with the buttons in the *Select* box. The box has a
   **Total** row (all runs) and a **Selected** row (only the rows you ticked):
   use the row that matches what you want.
   - **Accession List** → `SRR_Acc_List.txt`: one run per line. This is the
     input to the download scripts.
   - **Metadata** → `SraRunTable.csv` (older downloads: `.txt`): the full
     table.

   Your browser saves both into your computer's **Downloads** folder. The next
   section says where to move them.

### Columns of SraRunTable worth knowing

| Column | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| `Run` | The accession to download |
| `BioSample`, `Sample Name` / `GEO_Accession (exp)` | Which biological sample the run belongs to. **Several runs can share one** |
| `Experiment` | The library (SRX) |
| `LibraryLayout` | `PAIRED` or `SINGLE`: what files to expect |
| `LibrarySelection`, `LibrarySource`, `LibraryStrategy` | e.g. `cDNA`, `TRANSCRIPTOMIC`, `RNA-Seq`; confirms you have the right assay |
| `AvgSpotLen` | Average spot length: **read 1 + read 2** for paired data (126 = 2×63) |
| `Bases`, `Bytes` | Size: use `Bytes` to plan disk space ([fasterq-dump](fasterq-dump.qmd#disk-space)) |
| `Instrument` | e.g. `Illumina HiSeq 2000` |
| author columns (`treatment`, `cell_line`, `source_name`, ...) | The biology, as the submitters described it. Names vary between datasets |

::: {.callout-tip}
**Save `SraRunTable.csv` with your data.** It is the record of what each
file is, and you'll build your samplesheet from it.
:::

## Where to put the two files {#where-files-go}

Give **each dataset its own folder**, named after its accession, and put
`SRR_Acc_List.txt` and `SraRunTable.csv` **at the top of that folder**. That
folder is where you'll run every download command, and where the FASTQs end
up. Keep the guide's scripts in one place, cloned once:

```
~/download-public-data/           ← this guide's repository (the scripts), cloned once
~/public_data/                    ← all your public datasets (on a cluster: in scratch)
└── GSE52778/                     ← ONE folder per dataset, named by accession; run commands from here
    ├── SRR_Acc_List.txt          ← Run Selector "Accession List"
    ├── SraRunTable.csv           ← Run Selector "Metadata"
    ├── runs_to_samples.tsv       ← you make it: run → sample name
    ├── README.md                 ← paper, accession, date downloaded
    ├── sra/   tmp/               ← temporary; deleted after conversion
    ├── fastq/                    ← the downloaded FASTQs (+ read_counts.tsv)
    ├── merged/                   ← one pair per sample, named by sample
    └── logs/                     ← job logs (clusters)
```

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data.git ~/download-public-data   # once
mkdir -p ~/public_data/GSE52778 && cd ~/public_data/GSE52778                               # per dataset
```

On a cluster, put `public_data/` in your **scratch** space instead of `~`
(home folders are small): for example `mkdir -p /scratch/$USER/public_data/GSE52778`.

### Getting the files there

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart TD
  RS["Run Selector<br/>(in your web browser)"] -->|"click Accession List<br/>and Metadata"| DL["your laptop's<br/>Downloads folder"]
  DL -->|"working on this laptop"| M1["mv into the dataset folder"]
  DL -->|"working on a cluster"| M2["scp / rsync up<br/>to the dataset folder"]
  CLI["No browser?<br/>(e.g. already on the cluster)"] -->|"ENA API / Entrez Direct"| M3["create them directly<br/>in the dataset folder"]
  M1 & M2 & M3 --> DS["GSE52778/<br/>SRR_Acc_List.txt + SraRunTable.csv"]
  DS --> CHK["check them<br/>(below)"]
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Working on this computer

```bash
mv ~/Downloads/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/Downloads/SraRunTable.csv ~/public_data/GSE52778/
```

If you downloaded more than once, your browser may have named the newest
copies `SRR_Acc_List (1).txt` etc. Rename them as you move them:
`mv ~/Downloads/"SRR_Acc_List (1).txt" ~/public_data/GSE52778/SRR_Acc_List.txt`.

## Working on a cluster

Run this **on your laptop** (in a terminal on the laptop, not in your cluster
session), filling in your user name, the cluster's address and your dataset
folder there:

```bash
scp ~/Downloads/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/Downloads/SraRunTable.csv \
    <user>@<cluster address>:/scratch/<user>/public_data/GSE52778/
```

Or use a graphical file-transfer app (Cyberduck, FileZilla, MobaXterm, or your
cluster's web portal such as Open OnDemand) and drop the two files into the
dataset folder.

## Without a browser

Make both files directly where you are, from ENA (works for GEO/SRA projects too):

```bash
cd ~/public_data/GSE52778
curl -s "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=PRJNA229998&result=read_run&fields=run_accession,sample_accession,experiment_accession,sample_title,library_layout,read_count,base_count&format=tsv" > ena_runs.tsv
tail -n +2 ena_runs.tsv | cut -f1 > SRR_Acc_List.txt
```

`ena_runs.tsv` then plays the role of `SraRunTable.csv`. Or, with NCBI's
Entrez Direct: `esearch -db sra -query PRJNA229998 | efetch -format runinfo > SraRunTable.csv`
(one row per run; the run accessions are in its first column).
:::

### Check they arrived intact

```bash
cd ~/public_data/GSE52778
ls -l                         # both files, not 0 bytes
head -3 SRR_Acc_List.txt      # SRR... one per line
wc -l SRR_Acc_List.txt        # number of runs (should match the Run Selector count)
head -2 SraRunTable.csv       # a header line, then one run
```

If you only want some of the runs, edit `SRR_Acc_List.txt` (one accession per
line; `nano SRR_Acc_List.txt`), or download the **Selected** list instead. The
scripts in this guide ignore blank lines and Windows line endings.

Then write a two-line `README.md` in the same folder (the paper, the accession,
today's date). Future you will thank you.

## Option B: ENA (also gives direct FASTQ links)

Search the accession at [ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJNA229998).
The *Read Files* table lists every run with **direct `.fastq.gz` links and
MD5 checksums**. *Show Column Selection* adds fields such as `sample_title`;
*TSV* downloads the table. The same table is available from the ENA
**portal API**, which is easy to script:

```bash
curl -s "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=SRP033351&result=read_run&fields=run_accession,sample_title,library_layout,read_count,fastq_ftp,fastq_md5,fastq_bytes&format=tsv" \
  > SRP033351_ena.tsv
column -t -s $'\t' SRP033351_ena.tsv | cut -c1-120 | head
```

```
run_accession  sample_title       library_layout  read_count  fastq_ftp ...
SRR1039508     N61311_untreated   PAIRED          22935521    ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR103/008/SRR1039508/SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz;...
SRR1039509     N61311_Dex         PAIRED          21155707    ...
```

See [Downloading from ENA](ena.qmd) to get the FASTQs this way.

## Option C: the command line

**Entrez Direct** (NCBI's command-line tools; `conda install -c bioconda entrez-direct`,
or a cluster module) gives the same run table as Run Selector:

```bash
esearch -db sra -query PRJNA229998 | efetch -format runinfo > runinfo.csv
cut -d, -f1 runinfo.csv | grep -E '^[SED]RR' > SRR_Acc_List.txt
```

**pysradb** (a Python package, `pip install pysradb`) converts between
accession types and fetches metadata:

```bash
pysradb gse-to-srp GSE52778
pysradb metadata SRP033351 --detailed > SRP033351_metadata.tsv
```

## A checklist before downloading

- [ ] The assay is what you expect (`LibraryStrategy`, the GEO design).
- [ ] You know which runs belong to which biological sample.
- [ ] You know if it's paired or single-end (`LibraryLayout`).
- [ ] You know the read length (`AvgSpotLen`, halved for paired).
- [ ] If the paper says, note the library kit / strandedness (often only in
      the GEO *Extraction protocol* or *Library construction* fields).
- [ ] You've added up `Bytes` and have **10–20×** that free for the
      conversion step (or use ENA, which needs no conversion).
- [ ] The data are open access (not dbGaP/EGA).
